reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets doubled Aug-Sep 2026 (E-07) because, per the only surviving supported hypothesis (H-RULE-CHANGE), a change to billing import validation rules around August causes the billing system to compute or accept bills incorrectly on accounts with actual (non-estimated) meter reads, generating genuine billing errors that drive disputes. This is evidenced by disputed bills being dominated by ACTUAL-read bills (1785 of 3025, E-02), a pattern that estimate-substitution mechanisms (AMI vendor gaps, field manual-read gaps, staffing shortfall) cannot explain since they act only through estimate substitution, and it is not a response-speed problem since ticket response times are within the 3.0-day SLA (E-04).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Dispute tickets doubled from a ~600/month baseline to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-07). For the ESTIMATED-read subset of disputed bills (1240 of 3025, E-02), the dominant cause is a billing-import rejection: 1184 of these had an AMI read received before cutoff but were rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, forcing estimate substitution (E-11), coincident with validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) comparing raw register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-12), applied to AMI firmware v4.2 (rollout 2026-06) whose register output is in 0.1 m3 units versus legacy v3.x's whole-m3 units (E-13) — a mismatch that would make normal consumption appear tenfold inflated and be falsely flagged as high-consumption by BV-17. This mechanism explains only the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset; the majority of disputes occur on ACTUAL-read bills (1785 of 3025, E-02) and their cause is not yet identified by current evidence.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
